events.title: Storytime with Claire Wrenn Bobrow
events.description: Join us for a special storytime as author Claire Wrenn Bobrow returns to Linden Tree to share her delightful new picture book, Party Pony! Not another party! Parties used to be Pony's favorite—until every bash turned him into a work horse! Now Pony is a party pooper. How will Pony's friends show him he's worthy of a party too? For any kid who's ever felt left out, this witty picture book is a must-have for the home or school library, and it's perfect for gifting and reading at parties. Grab your copy and join the celebration!
events.blurb: Hear author Claire Wrenn Bobrow read her new picture book "Party Pony!" and find out why the pony has grown tired of parties.

events.title: Middle Grade Book Club: The Wish Ring Cipher
events.description: It's the next meeting of our middle grade book club for ages 9+! The club is led by bookseller extraordinaire Lorilee. We aim to introduce readers to new books they can discuss together in a fun, relaxed setting. This month's book is The Wish Ring Cipher by Alexandra Ott, a fast-paced adventure novel filled with puzzle-solving, a hint of magic, and new school fears. Please email lorilee@lindentreebooks.com to RSVP. Emma Avery has always loved solving puzzles and codes, and now that she's processing a recent autism diagnosis and facing down seventh grade at a new school, they're even more important to her. Then Emma meets Nate Lin. He's popular and funny and... loves codes, too. He introduces Emma to the Codebreakers, a group of his friends dedicated to cracking codes that have been discovered in the ruins of a nearby ghost town, which are believed to lead to magical objects. But they're not the only ones on the hunt, and when their sinister rivals close in on an object that grants unlimited wishes, the Codebreakers must race to beat them to it before they use it for dark magic.
events.attendanceNote: For readers ages 9 and older. Email the bookstore to RSVP using its events calendar.
events.blurb: Talk about The Wish Ring Cipher with fellow readers ages 9 and up at a middle grade book club led by bookseller Lorilee.

events.title: Girl Scout Program: Home Scientist (Brownies)
events.address: 201 S Market St, San Jose, CA 95113
events.description: Science is all around us! Brownies begin by making pepper dance using the amazing properties of electricity. Next, they become kitchen chemists and use pantry items to make art with delicious treats. Then they explore properties of density and use them to blow up a balloon without breath and make their own lava lamp. Finally, Brownies will learn how science can be used to make toys and make their very own silly putty! This program covers all five steps required to earn the Home Scientist Badge. Participants will receive the badge and a Tech fun patch at the end of the session.
events.blurb: Make pepper dance with electricity, then use pantry items as a kitchen chemist in this Brownies Home Scientist program.

events.title: Girl Scout Program: Tech Detective (Juniors and Cadettes)
events.address: 201 S Market St, San Jose, CA 95113
events.description: Do you have what it takes to be a Tech Detective? Juniors and Cadettes will begin by practicing the art of forensic drawing by sketching a "suspect" as described by a "key witness." Next, they learn about & practice codes and fingerprinting. Juniors will explore the role of DNA in forensics — what it is, what it does, and how it helps solve crimes. They then get to perform an experiment to extract real DNA, and finally use what they have learnt to identify someone from ancient DNA! This program covers all five steps required to earn the Juniors Detective badge or the Cadette Special Agent badge. Participants will receive the badge and a Tech fun patch at the end of the session.
events.blurb: Sketch a "suspect" from a key witness's description, then practice forensic drawing, codes, and fingerprinting as a Junior or Cadette Girl Scout.

events.title: Storytime with Sahar Shams
events.description: Join us for a special storytime as author Sahar Shams shares her festive debut picture book, What Does Santa Want for Christmas? Every year, children all around the world ask themselves what they'd like to receive from Santa. But one little boy has a different question: What would Santa wish for? Determined, Dorim sets out on a quest to craft the perfect present—but he'll need some help from his friends. With Christmas fast approaching, will they be able to make Santa's wish come true in time?

events.description: Note: The December 5th meditation session will be at the Palo Alto Art Center. This session is open to all ages. Children under 10 years old must be accompanied by an adult. Come and improve your mental and physical health in mindfulness meditation sessions led by Phuong Pham. Each session is 30 minutes of sitting meditation and 15 minutes of releasing meditation followed by 15 minutes of group sharing and Q&A. It is open to all levels of experience, and no registration is required. Participants are encouraged to bring their own yoga mats and/or meditation cushions. Chairs are available for those who do not bring them. Phuong is a Buddhist nun experienced in leading mindfulness meditation. See the library's event page to learn more about Phuong and find her videos on the library's YouTube channel.

events.title: Tech Mentor / Computer & iPad Assistance
events.description: A volunteer tech mentor offers 1-on-1 help with computer skills. Are you a senior trying to catch up with the digital world? Would you like to learn how to create an email, to search the internet, to create and edit Microsoft Word documents, to do online job searching or to complete online job applications? Increase your digital literacy today. Our tech mentors can guide you in learning a variety of computer skills that enable you to better use the library's public computers and to benefit from the library's freely available online resources, including ebooks! Don't worry about not having a computer; iPads will be available for in-library use during the mentoring session. You can drop in for help from the tech mentor. If you have more questions, please call us at 408-808-3053.
events.blurb: Get one-on-one computer and iPad help from a volunteer tech mentor who can help you build your skills.

events.title: One-on-One Reading Coach for Kids
events.description: Our One-on-One Reading Tutor for Kids provides students in grades K-3 with an opportunity to improve their reading skills by working one-on-one with a reading coach. Our reading coach creates a positive reading experience for beginning and developing readers and helps children build confidence as readers. Our reading coach will listen to children read and provide support in phonics, sight words, and comprehension. Students can bring their favorite book or choose from the available selection at the Cambrian Branch Library to read aloud to their reading coach. Free. No advance registration is required. Sessions last 15 minutes and are available on a first-come, first-served basis. (A slightly longer session may be permitted, provided there are no other participants.) If you'd like to use your reading session to reduce your library fines, tell your coach. This option is open to youth only. Please note that the One-On-One Reading Tutor for Kids is a program to encourage young readers to practice their reading skills with an adult volunteer. (It is not intended as an hour-long tutoring session.)
events.attendanceNote: Free. No advance registration is required. Sessions last 15 minutes and are available on a first-come, first-served basis. (A slightly longer session may be permitted, provided there are no other participants.)

events.title: 1-on-1 Tech Help / Asistencia Tecnológica
events.description: Get free one-on-one support with everyday tech questions. A Tech Mentor can help with basic smartphone, tablet, and computer tasks. Obtén apoyo gratuito y personalizado para tus preguntas tecnológicas del día a día. Un mentor tecnológico puede ayudarte con tareas básicas en teléfonos inteligentes, tabletas y computadoras. Por ejemplo, puede ayudarte a configurar y usar el correo electrónico, descargar y usar aplicaciones, hacer videollamadas con Zoom, FaceTime o Google Meet, navegar por internet, hacer búsquedas sencillas, consultar el sitio web y los recursos digitales de SJPL y usar la aplicación 311. events.title: Infant & Toddler Storytime
events.description: Come join us every Tuesday for Infant & Toddler Storytime! Infant & Toddler Storytime invites babies and their caregivers to learn together by strengthening their relationship with each other through stories, songs, bounces, tickles, rhymes, books, and play. After Storytime concludes, we invite you to Stay & Play! The Storytime librarian will join in the fun with special toys, giving babies and parents time to connect. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards. Free. Attendance limits follow SJPL guidelines.
events.blurb: Sing, bounce, and read along with your baby at Infant & Toddler Storytime.

events.title: Asistencia tecnológica y ayuda personalizada
events.description: ¿Estás cansado de no poder hacer cosas tecnológicas por ti mismo? ¿Cansado de esperar a que los miembros de tu familia te ayuden o hagan las cosas por ti? ¡Ahora puedes aprender a hacer todo eso por ti mismo! Tenemos personas pacientes y serviciales disponibles para ayudarte a aprender cualquier tema relacionado con la tecnología. Nunca es tarde para aprender a usar la tecnología. ¡Solo llámanos! La biblioteca te brindará apoyo para: Abrir una cuenta de correo electrónico; Conectarte a un punto de acceso o a una red Wi-Fi; Usar Chromebooks o computadoras; Usar Zoom; Encontrar clases de la biblioteca e inscribirte en ellas; Obtener una tarjeta de la biblioteca; Reservar materiales; Usar aplicaciones de la biblioteca; Usar un teléfono móvil; Buscar en internet. Este es un programa presencial organizado en la Sucursal de la Biblioteca Latinoamericana. El personal de la biblioteca o un voluntario estará allí para guiarte en todo, pero serás tú quien controle la computadora. Si no puedes asistir a tu cita, llama para cancelarla. Se dará prioridad a los clientes que no falten a sus citas. Gratis. Se requiere inscripción. Para inscribirte, llama al (408) 294-1237.
events.blurb: Get personalized tech help in Spanish at the Biblioteca Latinoamericana and practice doing the tasks yourself.

events.title: Family Storytime + Stay & Play
events.description: Storytime is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities such as stories, songs, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement activities. Storytime is a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of reading and learning for all ages. This program is geared for children of all ages and their parents/caregivers! After Storytime concludes, families are invited to Stay & Play! For 30 minutes after storytime, special, age-appropriate toys will be available to keep the fun going. The librarian will also be there to answer any questions, recommend books, and talk to families! Free, with limited capacity. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.
events.attendanceNote: Seating is first come, first served. The library hands out a limited number of tickets at the information desk 30 minutes before storytime.
events.blurb: Sing, rhyme, and play with your family at Village Square Library's storytime and stay-and-play session.

events.title: English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club
events.description: Berryessa Branch Library presents an in-person adult English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club. Are you looking for a place to practice your English conversation skills in a fun, welcoming and safe environment? Our English Language Learners (ELL) Conversation Club offers a respectful environment for adult learners of English to practice speaking English in everyday situations. Learners of all levels are welcome! Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Practice your English conversation skills with other learners in a welcoming club setting.

events.title: Art Instruction Series
events.address: 1243 San Tomas Aquino Rd. San Jose
events.description: This intensive 3-day series introduces children ages 12-14 to the fundamentals of character design. By blending structural anatomy with creative "shape language" and storytelling, students will learn how to build characters that feel alive, consistent, and purposeful. Students are expected to attend all sessions. Free. Registration recommended. Registered participants have priority, followed by walk-ins. The library provides some art supplies (sketch paper, HB pencils, and erasers). You may bring your own instead.
events.attendanceNote: The library gives registered participants priority and then takes walk-ins if space remains. The three-day series is for ages 12 to 14.
events.blurb: Sketch original characters in a 3-day series for ages 12-14, covering structural anatomy, shape language, and storytelling.

events.title: Educational Park Art Club
events.description: This week, in celebration of Native American Heritage Month, we'll learn about Jaune Quick-to-See Smith, an artist and enrolled citizen of the Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes. Then we'll use what we've learned to make art of our own. Join us every Tuesday as we learn about an artist or art style, then make art of our own. Recommended for ages 5-12. November Events: November 3 - Frank Buffalo Hyde (drawing); November 10 - Rangoli (Diwali craft); November 17 - Theresa Secord (weaving); November 24 - Jaune Quick-to-See Smith (map art). Free. No registration is required.
events.blurb: Learn about artist Jaune Quick-to-See Smith for Native American Heritage Month, then make your own art at the library's club.

events.title: ESL Classes with Evergreen Valley College (EVC) 502: Listening & Speaking
events.description: ESL Listening & Speaking 1 is a noncredit course for high-beginning English learners. Students will learn to pronounce basic words accurately, communicate effectively, understand and use basic grammar structures, and build their foundational vocabulary. Complete Guided Self-Placement before enrolling so the college can help you choose the right ESL level. For accurate results, complete the assessment on your own in a quiet setting. Submit the registration form. To schedule your assessment appointment, send an email to marcela.guevara@sjlibrary.org. ESL 502 runs from August 25, 2026, through December 10, 2026. Classes meet Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday from 5:15 PM to 6:45 PM. The instructor is to be determined. Space is limited.
events.attendanceNote: Space is limited.
events.blurb: Build pronunciation, basic grammar, and foundational vocabulary in a non-credit, high-beginning ESL Listening & Speaking class with Evergreen Valley College.

events.title: Family Storytime + Stay & Play
events.description: Storytime is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities such as stories, songs, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement activities. Storytime is a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of reading and learning for all ages. This program is geared for children of all ages and their parents/caregivers! After storytime, families can Stay & Play with a variety of toys in the Children's Area. Free, with limited capacity. Please note that this will be an indoor program. Seating for Storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis. San José Public Library Storytimes are in alignment with the City's Education and Digital Literacy Initiative.
events.attendanceNote: Seating for Storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis.
events.blurb: Bring the whole family to sing songs, share stories and rhymes, and try fingerplays and movement activities at Alviso Library.

events.title: Bilingual Hindi-English Storytime / द्विभाषी हिंदी-अंग्रेज़ी कहानी समय
events.description: The Almaden Branch Library invites you to a bilingual Hindi-English storytime for the community. This special storytime helps children strengthen their language comprehension skills while enjoying traditional rhymes and stories from Indian culture. Offered monthly, this program is intended for children ages 3-10 and their families, but all ages and language abilities are welcome to join! Free. No registration required. अल्माडेन ब्रांच पुस्तकालय समुदाय के लिए हिंदी-अंग्रेज़ी द्विभाषी कहानी समय में आपका हार्दिक स्वागत करता है। यह विशेष कहानी समय बच्चों को भारतीय संस्कृति की पारंपरिक कविताओं और कहानियों का आनंद लेते हुए उनकी भाषा समझने की क्षमताओं को मजबूत करने में मदद करता है। यह कार्यक्रम महीने में एक बार आयोजित किया जाता है और 3-10 साल के बच्चों और उनके परिवारों के लिए लक्षित है, लेकिन सभी उम्र और भाषा क्षमताओं के लोग इसमें शामिल हो सकते हैं! मुफ़्त, किसी भी आरक्षण की आवश्यकता नहीं!
events.blurb: Hear stories read in both Hindi and English at Almaden Library's bilingual storytime for the community on Tuesday evening.

events.title: Bridge Card Game
events.description: Bridge is great exercise for your brain! This bridge program is designed for adults who are passionate about bridge and are looking to enhance their game with regular practice and social interaction. The atmosphere is relaxed and welcoming, making it an ideal setting to engage with fellow bridge enthusiasts and to refine your strategies. Participants should know bridge terminology and have experience playing a hand. No instruction or assistance will be provided. Free. Seating is limited, and registration is required. This program is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Cambrian Library!
events.blurb: Play bridge with fellow adults who enjoy the game, with regular practice and social interaction.

events.title: Crochet Workshop: Hand Crochet Chunky Scarf
events.description: Mt. Pleasant Neighborhood Library will host a crochet workshop to create a chunky scarf. Adults of all skill levels are welcome. No registration is required. Space is available on a first-come, first-served basis. Materials are limited to 8 participants. Provided materials include Bernat Jumbo and Chunky yarns for hand crochet. Participants are welcome to bring their own materials. Please park on nearby streets while the library shares the elementary school's parking lot.
events.attendanceNote: Registration not required. Space is available on a first-come, first-served basis. Materials are limited to 8 participants. Provided materials include Bernat Jumbo and Chunky yarns for hand crochet. Participants are welcome to bring their own materials.
events.blurb: Make a chunky scarf by hand at this adults-only crochet workshop, open to all skill levels on a first-come, first-served basis.

events.title: Asistencia para buscar trabajo y crear un resumen (currículum)
events.description: ¿Necesita ayuda con su currículum o para buscar oportunidades de empleo? Reúnase personalmente con un miembro del personal de la biblioteca (uno a uno) para aprender cómo: Crear o actualizar su currículum; Navegar por sitios web de solicitudes de empleo; Completar formularios de solicitud de empleo; Aprender técnicas de entrevista; Obtener ayuda para registrarse en ServSafe (tarjeta para manipuladores de alimentos); *Desafortunadamente, no podemos ayudar con ninguna información personal/sensible (por ejemplo, número de seguro social, información bancaria, formularios de impuestos, etc.). Este es un programa presencial organizado en la Sucursal de la Biblioteca Latinoamericana. El personal de la biblioteca le guiará. Usted manejará la computadora. Gratis. Se requiere registro. Para registrarse, llame al (408) 294-1237.
events.blurb: Recibe ayuda para crear tu currículum y buscar oportunidades de empleo.

events.title: Social Workers in the Library Drop-In Hours
events.description: Advice, information, and referrals. Social Workers in the Library offers free social service information and referrals*. Our staff can meet with you, approach your needs without judgement, and help you find where to go for shelter, food, showers, mental health services, legal help, and more. Free. No registration required. *Disclaimer: SJPL's Social Work in the Library does not establish a social worker-client relationship. SJPL does not offer case management or extensive follow-up services. We will try our best to get you connected to any resource we know of that could suit your needs. Asesoramiento, información y referencias. Este programa ofrece información y referencias de servicios sociales gratuitos. Nuestro personal puede reunirse con usted, abordar sus necesidades sin juicio y ayudarle a encontrar dónde ir para obtener refugio, comida, duchas, servicios de salud mental, ayuda legal y más. Gratis. No se requiere registro. *Aviso: El Trabajo Social en la Biblioteca de SJPL no establece una relación de Trabajador Social-Cliente. SJPL no ofrece gestión de casos ni servicios de seguimiento extensos. Haremos todo lo posible por conectarte con cualquier recurso que conozcamos y que pueda satisfacer tus necesidades. Tư vấn, thông tin và giới thiệu. Nhân Viên Xã Hội trong Thư Viện cung cấp miễn phí thông tin về những dịch vụ xã hội và giới thiệu. Nhân viên của chúng tôi có thể gặp gỡ bạn, tiếp cận với nhu cầu của bạn mà không đánh giá, và giúp bạn tìm những nơi để đến trú ẩn, thực phẩm, tắm rửa, những dịch vụ sức khoẻ tâm thần, trợ giúp pháp lý, và nhiều hơn nữa. Miễn phí. Không bắt buộc phải đăng ký. Từ chối trách nhiệm: Nhân Viên Xã Hội của SJPL trong Thư Viện không thiết lập mối quan hệ giữa một nhân viên xã hội và khách hàng. SJPL không cung cấp quản lý các trường hợp hoặc dịch vụ theo dõi mở rộng. Chúng tôi sẽ cố gắng hết sức để kết nối bạn với bất kỳ nguồn nào chúng tôi biết có thể phù hợp với nhu cầu của bạn.
events.blurb: Stop by the drop-in table at Tully Library to ask a social worker for free social service information and referrals.

events.title: ELL Beginning English: The Basics
events.description: Do you want to build your English-language skills and your confidence? English Language Learners (ELL) can increase their English skills with our tutor in a welcoming and respectful environment for adult learners. Sessions take place on the 2nd and 4th Tuesdays. Topics may include learning new vocabulary, practicing pronunciation, and basic grammar. Suggested for English language learners with little to no experience. Space is limited and registration is required. Please stop by the Vineland Library or call us at (408) 808-3000 to register. Vineland's English Learning series: ELL Beginning English: A beginner program for learners with limited English skills; approximately levels 0-2; ELL Grammar and Vocabulary Club: An intermediate program for learners that know some English but want to learn more complex English; approximately levels 2-3; ELL Conversation Club: An advanced program for learners to practice speaking and listening while also learning about American culture and idioms; approximately levels 3-4; ELL Writing Club: A program where English learners at levels from high beginner to advanced can learn and practice their English writing skills; approximately levels 2-4.
events.attendanceNote: Space is limited and registration is required.
events.blurb: Practice basic English with a tutor in a welcoming adult class held on the second and fourth Tuesdays.

events.title: Family Storytime
events.description: Storytime is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities such as stories, songs, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement activities. Storytime is a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of reading and learning for all ages. This program is geared for children of all ages and their parents/caregivers! Storytime is free, and space is limited. Seating for Storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis. The library publishes conflicting ticket pickup instructions (60 or 30 minutes before storytime). Confirm pickup timing with Willow Glen Library. If the first session reaches 50 participants, the library will hold a second session. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.
events.attendanceNote: Seating for Storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis. The library's description says ticket pickup starts 60 minutes before storytime. Its signup instructions say 30 minutes. Confirm pickup timing with Willow Glen Library.
events.blurb: Join the whole family for stories, songs, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement activities at a mixed-age storytime on Tuesday morning.

events.title: Đọc truyện song ngữ & Thủ công | Bilingual Storytime & Craft
events.description: Giờ đọc truyện song ngữ Anh-Việt được tổ chức tại Thư Viện Evergreen, 2635 Aborn Road, San Jose, nhằm thúc đẩy các hoạt động đọc viết sớm qua các câu chuyện, bài hát, múa ca và vận động cơ thể. Chương trình này dành cho trẻ em ở mọi lứa tuổi cùng với cha mẹ hoặc người chăm sóc trẻ! Sau phần kể chuyện, các bé sẽ được hướng dẫn làm một món thủ công đơn giản và sáng tạo để mang về nhà! Hoàn toàn miễn phí, không cần đăng ký trước. Bilingual Storytime in English and Vietnamese, hosted by Evergreen Branch Library, will promote early literacy with stories, songs, fingerplay and movement activities. Children of all ages and their parents or caregivers are welcome. After storytime, children will learn to make a simple craft to take home. The program is free. No registration is required.
events.attendanceNote: All participants need a storytime ticket. The library hands out a limited number at the information desk 30 minutes before the program.
events.blurb: Join a bilingual English-Vietnamese storytime at Evergreen Library with stories, songs, and movement, followed by a craft, on Tuesday afternoon.

events.title: Digital Skills: One-On-One Tech Help for Seniors
events.description: The Almaden Branch offers 30-minute tech help appointments. Get help using Libby from OverDrive to read ebooks and listen to audiobooks, finding ebooks from Enki, reading the New York Times and the San Jose Mercury News online, or accessing and searching Consumer Reports. You can also get help learning a language with Mango, connecting to Wi-Fi or a hotspot, or using Discover & Go to reserve free or reduced-price tickets to local museums and attractions. Other topics include navigating the SJPL website, checking out a 7-day pass to Great Courses through Libby, using the library's pay-to-print system, and working through a Digital Skills Building Pathways lesson. By appointment only. One appointment per week per person. For questions, please call (408) 808-3040 or send an email to ab.sjpl@sjlibrary.org.
events.attendanceNote: By appointment only. One appointment per week per person. For questions, please call (408) 808-3040 or send an email to ab.sjpl@sjlibrary.org.
events.blurb: Seniors can bring their technology questions to Almaden Library for one-on-one help.

events.title: Bilingual Toddler Storytime / Tiempo de Cuentos & Stay and Play
events.description: Bilingual Toddler Storytime is designed for toddlers to engage in early literacy activities such as stories, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement. While the program is geared toward children ages 1–3, all children ages 0–5 are welcome to attend. After Storytime concludes, families are invited to Stay & Play. For 30 minutes following Storytime, special age-appropriate toys will be available for children and caregivers to continue the fun together: Storytime: 11:30 a.m. to noon; Stay & Play: noon to 12:30 p.m. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards. Tiempo de Cuentos & Stay and Play: Tiempo de Cuentos está diseñado para niños pequeños e invita a toda la familia a participar en actividades de alfabetización temprana, como cuentos, rimas, juegos con los dedos y actividades de movimiento. Después de que concluya el Tiempo de Cuentos, las familias están invitadas a quedarse y jugar. Durante 30 minutos después del Tiempo de Cuentos, habrá juguetes especiales y apropiados para cada edad disponibles para continuar la diversión. Tiempo de cuentos: 11:30 a.m. - 12:00 p.m.; Stay & Play: 12:00 p.m. - 12:30 p.m. Este programa ha sido diseñado en alineación con los Estándares de Calidad de la Educación Infantil.
events.blurb: Sing, rhyme, and play with your toddler during this bilingual early literacy storytime.

events.title: Baby Bouncers Lapsit for Prewalkers
events.description: Join us on Tuesday mornings for Baby Bouncers Lapsit (for non-walking babies up to 12 months old). This is a program for babies and caregivers with an early literacy focus on traditional nursery rhymes, lap bounces, body rhymes, songs, and very short and simple picture books. Caregivers are welcome to bring a blanket for their babies to lie on. Baby Bouncers Lapsit lasts 15 to 20 minutes. Caregivers are welcome to attend our Stay and Play session after the program. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3947, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Bounce, sing nursery rhymes, and share short picture books with your prewalking baby Tuesday mornings.

events.title: Los Altos Adult Book Discussion
events.description: Join us for our monthly book club meeting to discuss mostly contemporary (and occasional classic) fiction titles. Space is limited. Regular attendees do not need to register. Email Laura.Pasternack@lib.sccgov.org to receive monthly reminders and get permission to pick up copies of the books. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3947, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.attendanceNote: Join us for our monthly book club meeting to discuss mostly contemporary (and occasional classic) fiction titles. Space is limited. Regular attendees do not need to register. Email Laura.Pasternack@lib.sccgov.org to receive monthly reminders and get permission to pick up copies of the books.
events.blurb: Discuss the month's chosen contemporary or classic fiction title with fellow readers at this monthly book club.

events.title: Goodnight, Little Storytime
events.description: Please join us for our evening storytime! There will be songs, silliness, and (of course) stories. Pajamas are welcome. Free, with limited capacity. Vehicle parking may be limited. Space to park strollers outside the Children's Room is limited. Please leave strollers outside during storytime. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3947, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Wear your pajamas and enjoy evening songs and stories at this family storytime.

events.title: Music & Movement Storytime
events.description: Join us for music, stories, and joyful play at this storytime perfect for families with young children. Music and movement help our littlest learners develop their communication skills, their imagination, and their connection with the loving grown-ups in their lives. Let's sing! Free, with limited capacity. Vehicle parking may be limited. Space to park strollers outside the Children's Room is limited. Please leave strollers outside during storytime. This storytime will be noisy with singing, instruments, and pre-recorded music. Let the librarian know before storytime begins if you would like to borrow a pair of ear defenders for your child. This storytime is usually very busy with lots of families moving around. This storytime sometimes includes the use of soft scarves, weighted beanbags, and other textured items. Children are always free to skip these activities if they prefer. Need a social story? Email charlie.roos@lib.sccgov.org to request a digital social story to help your child feel prepared for storytime. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3947, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Sing, move, and play with your little ones at this music-filled storytime for families.

events.title: To Be Read Book Club for Grades 6-8
events.description: Join our book club! The To Be Read Book Club is for anyone in 6th, 7th or 8th grade this school year. We are reading Stargirl by Jerry Spinelli for our meeting on Tuesday, November 24th, from 4 to 5 p.m. in the Orchard Room at Los Altos Library. If you can attend, register online and pick up your copy of the book at the Children's Reference Desk at either Los Altos or Woodland Library. Please read the book before our meeting. At the meeting, we will discuss the book and do a fun activity. Snacks will be provided. Many thanks to the Friends of the Los Altos Library for making this program possible. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3947, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Students in grades 6–8 discuss Stargirl at Los Altos Library.
events.attendanceNote: Register online, then pick up Stargirl at the Children's Reference Desk at Los Altos or Woodland Library and read it before the meeting.

events.title: Fall Crafts for Grades K-5
events.description: Children in grades K to 5 are invited to celebrate fall with us by making fall-inspired crafts at the Milpitas Library. All materials will be provided. Registration opens November 13 at 3:30 PM. Thank you to the Friends of the Milpitas Library for making this program possible. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3947, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Make fall-inspired crafts with materials provided at the Milpitas Library, in a program for children in grades K to 5.

events.title: Vintage Media Lab
events.description: Preserve your old photographs, home movies, records and cassettes! How to Access: Check the Vintage Media Lab page. If appointments are still available for the month, click the Book@Rinconada button near the top of the page. Otherwise, check back on the first Monday of the month for another chance to sign up. Each appointment includes a skilled volunteer or staff person to assist you. Appointments are limited to a single two-hour appointment per week per person. Because space and time in the Vintage Media Lab are limited, we appreciate your cooperation in regard to equipment, storage and cleanliness. What to Bring: Laptop; SD Card, Memory Card; USB Drive, Flash Drive or Memory Stick; External Hard Drive; Your Vintage Media!
events.attendanceNote: Space is limited! Check the Vintage Media Lab page to see if appointments are still available for the month.
events.blurb: Book a session at Rinconada Library to digitize old photos, home movies, records, and cassettes.

events.title: Drop-in Tech Help
events.description: Stuck with a technology question? Need help with an ongoing issue or learning something new? Stop by the Rinconada branch library for our drop-in tech help Tuesday mornings. Staff can show you how to use Libby or Hoopla, access library databases and services, download and stream content, navigate the City of Palo Alto Library website, and download and use the new PACL app. They can also help with Wi-Fi, printing, setting up an email account, basic computer skills, and installing and using common apps. Unfortunately, helping you fix damaged hardware or software is not within our scope. Help is given on a first-come, first-served basis. Please bring any devices you use, make sure they are charged, and have your necessary passwords. We look forward to helping you.
events.attendanceNote: Help is given on a first-come, first-served basis. Please bring any devices you use, make sure they are charged, and have your necessary passwords. We look forward to helping you.
events.blurb: Bring your technology questions to Rinconada Library for drop-in help on Tuesday mornings.

events.title: ESL Classes with Evergreen Valley College (EVC) - ESL 501: Reading & Writing 1
events.description: ESL 501 Reading & Writing 1 is a free, noncredit course for learners at the high-beginning English level. It focuses on basic reading, writing, grammar, and vocabulary, with practice in speaking, listening, and pronunciation. Students learn the meanings of common words in context, express ideas in writing using familiar phrases and sentences, understand basic grammar structures, and read simplified texts. The instructor is Michelle N. Henninger.
events.blurb: Practice speaking, listening, reading, writing, pronunciation, and grammar in Evergreen Valley College's free, noncredit ESL Reading & Writing 1 course for beginners.

events.title: Playdates for Children and Their Caregivers
events.description: Join us for playdates every Wednesday. Children can practice sharing, taking turns, imitating others at play, and focusing together on an activity. Caregivers get a chance to connect. Don't miss out on this chance to celebrate the joys of play while connecting with other families in the community. It's a wonderful way to learn through play and create lasting memories together! 1st Wednesday: Cars; 2nd Wednesday: Superhero Obstacle Course (ages 3-8); 3rd Wednesday: LEGO Duplo Blocks; 4th Wednesday: Cars; 5th Wednesday: LEGO Duplo Blocks. Recommended for children ages 2–6.
events.blurb: Bring your child to Seven Trees Library and practice sharing, turn-taking, and play with other families.

events.title: Family Movie Club: Wonder
events.description: Please join us for Family Movie Club at the Joyce Ellington Branch Library as we watch Wonder, a movie that follows August Pullman, a 10-year-old boy born with facial differences, as he attends a mainstream school for the first time and inspires his classmates and community to choose kindness. Families are invited to relax and enjoy this fun movie together in a welcoming community setting. Popcorn will be provided, and we will have coloring pages available for those who prefer a quiet activity during the movie. Free. No registration required. The program is sponsored by the Friends of the Joyce Ellington Library.
events.blurb: Watch Wonder, the story of 10-year-old August Pullman starting at a mainstream school, at the library's Family Movie Club.

events.title: Tech Mentor: One-on-One Computer Help
events.address: 1102 E Santa Clara St San Jose
events.description: Confused by your computer? Get personalized tech assistance. Help is available for basic tasks such as printing, using email, connecting to Wi-Fi, creating documents, and accessing library resources. Registering for an appointment is optional. If you register for an appointment, it can start at any time between 3 p.m. and 4:30 p.m. Please contact Sarah Kishler at sarah.kishler@sjlibrary.org or 408-808-3075 to let us know what time you would like to come in. When there is space, walk-ins starting between 3 p.m. and 4:30 p.m. are also welcome.
events.attendanceNote: Appointments are optional. Walk-ins may start between 3 and 4:30 PM if space is available.
events.blurb: Get personalized help with printing, email, Wi-Fi, documents, or library resources on your computer.

events.title: 1-on-1 Tech Help
events.description: By appointment only. Do you need help using the computer? Don't know how to send an email or set up a Zoom meeting? Our tech mentor can help! Learn to open an email account, connect to Wi-Fi or a hotspot, use laptops or Chromebooks, and work in Microsoft Office. A mentor can also help you fill out simple forms online, use social media, and navigate the SJPL website. Free. Registration required. Availability is not guaranteed. For more information or to make an appointment, please call the branch at (408) 808-3077 or email eric.debold@sjlibrary.org.
events.attendanceNote: By appointment only.
events.blurb: Get one-on-one help from a tech mentor with computer basics, sending email, or setting up a Zoom meeting, by appointment only.

events.title: Baby Lap-Sit Story Time
events.description: This program is geared for pre-walking children and their parents or caregivers. Baby Lap-Sit Storytime invites newborns, infants, and their caregivers to learn together by strengthening their relationship with each other through stories, songs, bounces, tickles, rhymes, books, and play. The program includes 20-25 minutes of stories and songs, followed by 40 minutes of open play with age-appropriate toys. All attendees will be required to observe the library's Safety Guidelines. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.
events.blurb: Bring your pre-walking baby to listen to stories and rhymes built for little ones.

events.title: One-on-One Tech Help (English or Tiếng Việt)
events.description: Offered in English or Tiếng Việt. Do you need help using a computer? Want to set up an email account? Stop by the Santa Teresa Branch Library for a session with our experienced volunteer! They can help you set up an email account, write and send emails, use attachments, search the web, and enter data. They can also help you learn the basics of Microsoft Word, Excel, or web tools such as Google Docs, use the library's pay-for-print and photocopy machines, or download apps on your phone or tablet. You are welcome to bring your own device, such as a laptop, phone or tablet, or you can use one of our computers. Free. No registration required.
events.attendanceNote: Drop-ins subject to availability.
events.blurb: Sit down with a volunteer at Santa Teresa Library for computer or email help in English or Tiếng Việt.

events.title: Art Instruction Series
events.address: 1243 San Tomas Aquino Rd. San Jose
events.description: This intensive 3-day series introduces children ages 12-14 to the fundamentals of character design. By blending structural anatomy with creative "shape language" and storytelling, students will learn how to build characters that feel alive, consistent, and purposeful. Students are expected to attend all sessions. Free. Registration recommended. Registered participants have priority, followed by walk-ins. The library provides some art supplies (sketch paper, HB pencils, and erasers). You may bring your own instead.
events.attendanceNote: The library gives registered participants priority and then takes walk-ins if space remains. The three-day series is for ages 12 to 14.
events.blurb: Sketch original characters in a 3-day series for ages 12-14, covering structural anatomy, shape language, and storytelling.

events.title: Reading Buddy in English & Spanish
events.description: Help your child build confidence and strengthen their English or Spanish reading skills in a fun and supportive environment! Children in kindergarten through 3rd grade are invited to read aloud in English or Spanish to trained teen volunteers who will offer encouragement and help with pronunciation when needed. Whether your child is a fluent English or Spanish reader or is still building their confidence, Reading Buddy in English and Spanish provides a welcoming space to practice reading skills, celebrate bilingual literacy, and foster a lifelong love of reading—especially for students enrolled in dual-language immersion programs. Recommended for: Children in grades K–3 and their caregivers. Please note: Caregivers must remain in the Children's Area during the program.
events.blurb: Read aloud in English or Spanish to trained teen volunteers at Willow Glen Library's Reading Buddy program.

events.title: Robotics Workshop: Presented by Power Beans Foundation
events.description: In this full-day workshop with the Power Beans Foundation, participants will learn the principles of robot design and engineering, along with teamwork and collaboration skills. Teams will build VEX V5RC robots, program them with VEXcode, and showcase them in a friendly competition near the end. Lunch is from noon to 12:30 p.m. Please bring your own lunch. Participants need a signed waiver before taking part. You'll receive a copy by email. Copies will also be available when you arrive. Participants must be at least 10 years old. Registration is required. Registered participants will receive a detailed agenda. Registration opens November 4, 2026, at 9 a.m.
events.attendanceNote: Ages 10 and up. Bring lunch and complete a signed waiver before participating.
events.blurb: Build and program robots in a hands-on workshop with the Power Beans Foundation, working with VEX V5RC parts and VEXcode.

events.title: Infant & Toddler Storytime

events.description: Infant and Toddler Storytime invites children and their caregivers to wiggle, rhyme, and sing with diverse books, songs, and fingerplays that encourage language, play, and exploration. Until 12 PM, the Storytime librarian and special toys will be on the Children's Room floor to keep the fun going. Meet new friends, play with toys, chat, get book recommendations, and maybe even create something! Storytime: 11:00-11:30 AM; Stay & Play: 11:30 AM-12:00 PM. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.
events.blurb: Wiggle, rhyme, and sing with your infant or toddler through books and fingerplays at this storytime.

events.title: English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club: Intermediate
events.description: ¡Ven a practicar hablar y escuchar inglés en persona en la Biblioteca Latinoamericana! Cada sesión está dirigida por personal de la biblioteca que habla español e inglés. Gratis. No es necesario registrarse. Come practice speaking and listening in English in person at the Biblioteca Latinoamericana! No registration required.

ESL 502 runs from August 25, 2026, through December 10, 2026. Classes meet Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday from 5:15 PM to 6:45 PM. The instructor is to be determined. We will assist you with the application and registration processes in person at the Educational Park Branch Library. Space is limited.

events.description: Be part of a fun volunteering opportunity for teens between the ages of 13 and 18. events.title: TeenHQ MakerSpace Studio
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Middle and high schoolers: Come explore the TeenHQ MakerSpace! Up to 5 teens at a time can use our 3D printers, a poster printer, a Glowforge laser cutter, sewing machines and sergers, a Cricut, a button press, and assorted craft supplies. Work with our teen librarian to bring your idea to life. Equipment and materials have limits and time requirements. All services are provided for free to middle and high school students (grades 6-12). Younger people and adults are not permitted in the area unless required to assist with a disability. The area is wheelchair accessible from the Children's Room elevator. Other accommodations can be made available upon request. Allow enough time to set up the equipment and work on your project. If your work takes longer than one studio session, you may need to come back to pick up a finished item or continue the project at another session. We appreciate your patience and flexibility. 3D Printing: All requested prints must take less than 4.5 hours to print. All requested prints will need to be picked up at a later date. Contact information is required for notification of pick-up. 3D print quality and the time needed to complete prints are not guaranteed. Multiple objects can be printed as long as the total time does not exceed 4.5 hours. Poster Printing: Set up your design on a 24 × 36-inch canvas and save it as a PNG file. Please see the regularly scheduled poster printing event for further details. One poster per teen per day. Glowforge: Create a custom engraved object. Follow guidelines similar to those for the Custom Keychain Program. The librarian decides how complex a request can be. Sewing & Serger Machines: It is recommended that you bring your own fabric and thread if fabric is special or color is a factor. Scrap material and thread are available, but we cannot guarantee material quality or availability. An iron and ironing board are also available. Cricut: Basic Cricut supplies are available, such as construction and cardstock paper. If your project is specialized, such as requiring iron-on, you'll need to bring your own materials. It is recommended that you know the requirements for any materials you provide. Button Press: TeenHQ offers two sizes of button presses. We cannot offer printing. If you bring your own printout of buttons, it must be printed on standard printer paper. Paper thicker than standard printer paper cannot be used on the button presses. All measurements below are diameters in inches. Small Button Press: 1.25"; Large Button Press: 2.25"; Picture Size: 1.156"; Cut Line: 1.629"; Picture Size: 2.063"; Cut Line: 2.625".
events.attendanceNote: The event page has no signup link. Space is limited to five teens. Check with TeenHQ for availability.
events.blurb: Use the TeenHQ MakerSpace at King Library to work with 3D printers, a Glowforge, sewing machines, a Cricut, and a button press.

events.title: Digital Skills: One-On-One Tech Help for Seniors
events.description: The Almaden Branch offers 30-minute tech help appointments. Get help using Libby from OverDrive to read ebooks and listen to audiobooks, finding ebooks from Enki, reading the New York Times and the San Jose Mercury News online, or accessing and searching Consumer Reports. You can also get help learning a language with Mango, connecting to Wi-Fi or a hotspot, or using Discover & Go to reserve free or reduced-price tickets to local museums and attractions. events.title: Hindi for Everyday Life
events.description: This is an interactive, structured program designed for children ages 5-12 who would like to learn Hindi. It is perfectly tailored for learners from all backgrounds, whether they hear Hindi at home or are exploring it for the very first time. The curriculum nurtures the four core language skills—speaking, listening, reading, and writing—in alignment with US Academic Standards and the California World Languages Framework. Children will learn through physical workbooks, worksheets and short audio/visual tools provided for the program, ensuring a rich and engaging experience. Children must be accompanied by an adult caregiver during this workshop.

events.title: Easy Tech Seniors
events.description: Learn new skills in a relaxed and interactive group setting! Easy Tech Seniors is led by Malhar, a local high school student with a passion for helping senior citizens embrace technology to enrich their daily lives. For the best experience, we recommend bringing your own mobile device, but you can also follow the demonstration on the projector screen and take notes. 2026 Topics: Jan 24th - Library apps for reading e-books - an overview of SJPL's e-book collections on the library website, with a focus on Libby from OverDrive - How to adjust reading settings like text size and lighting, and how to use the audiobook controls. If time allows, the session will also cover Hoopla. Feb 28th - Using Zoom for Meetings and Social Connection - How to join meetings confidently or host simple meetings. Learn to mute and unmute audio or video and use the chat. Troubleshooting basics will also be covered. Mar 28th - Using ChatGPT - How to use ChatGPT to summarize long documents, organize items like receipts, ask effective questions and protect your privacy. Using ChatGPT responsibly will also be covered. April 25th - Managing contacts effectively and setting reminders - Add and organize contacts on your device. Create groups (family, emergency). Back up and sync safely. Set recurring reminders for daily tasks. Integrate reminders with calendars. May 23rd - Demystifying AI. June 27th - Spotting AI Scams and Fake Messages. July 25th - Emergency Features on Smartphones. August 22nd - Google Translate for Travel and Communication - Use text, voice, and camera translation. Save common phrases for travel. Practice offline translation. September 26th - Using ChatGPT - How to use ChatGPT to summarize long documents, organize items like receipts, ask effective questions and protect your privacy. Using ChatGPT responsibly will also be covered. October 24th - How to Make Your Phone Easier to See - Adjusting text size, using the magnifier, voice to text, and dark mode. On November 28, learn to turn on and use Siri or Google Assistant. Practice checking the weather, setting timers, and making calls. You'll also learn to manage privacy settings and shortcuts. There is no program in December. The class is free and limited to 10 attendees. Registration is recommended. Walk-ins are welcome if space is available.
events.attendanceNote: Online reservations are recommended. Walk-ins are welcome if space is available.

events.title: Queer Cafe - Cozy Vibes Edition
events.description: Queer joy shall abound at the Queer Café! Let's grab our chunky knit sweaters, a warm cup of something pumpkin-spiced, and celebrate the fall season for November's Queer Cafe. Queer Cafe is an LGBTQ+-friendly space in our community room for folks to gather, read, craft, and chat. A selection of queer reading materials will be available to browse and check out. In addition to light snacks and refreshments, we'll have craft supplies and a selection of cozy and found family reads highlighting queer characters and authors. While the intention of this program is to create a safe and comfortable space for patrons identifying as LGBTQ+, we welcome all participants and reading materials. ¡La alegría queer estará presente en cada rincón del Café Queer! ¡Pongámonos nuestros suéteres gruesos de punto, disfrutemos de una bebida calientita con especias de calabaza y celebremos la temporada de otoño en el Café Queer de noviembre! El Café Queer es un espacio acogedor para la comunidad LGBTQ+ en nuestra sala comunitaria, donde las personas pueden reunirse, leer, hacer manualidades y conversar. Habrá una selección de libros y otros materiales de lectura con temática LGBTQ+ disponibles para explorar y llevar en préstamo. Además de bocadillos y bebidas ligeras, tendremos materiales para manualidades y una selección de lecturas reconfortantes, incluidas historias sobre familias elegidas, que destacan a personajes y autores LGBTQ+. Se anima a las personas participantes a compartir y conocer a otros lectores con intereses similares, pero no se les pedirá que revelen su identidad ni sus preferencias de lectura. Aunque el propósito de este programa es crear un espacio seguro y cómodo para las personas que se identifican como LGBTQ+, todas las personas y todos los materiales de lectura son bienvenidos.

events.title: Korean Calligraphy Workshop: Writing Your Name in Hangul with Flow and Rhythm
events.description: In this 90-minute workshop, participants will use calligraphy brushes, ink, and hanji paper to write their names in Hangul. Because Hangul is based on sound, names from many different languages can be written in Hangul according to how they are pronounced. Participants will see how their names look in Hangul and experience the rhythm of Korean writing through brush movement and repetition. Participants can get help writing their names in Hangul along the way. We will begin with simple brush exercises on hanji paper. Participants will practice moving the whole arm, changing the pressure and speed of the brush, and making different kinds of lines. They will then write their names several times, following the movement and rhythm of each brushstroke. At the end of the workshop, participants will write their names on a hanji fan. No previous calligraphy or Korean language experience is needed. Instructor: Sang-ah Choi. Materials: All materials will be provided, including calligraphy brushes, ink, hanji paper, and one hanji fan for each participant. Duration: 90 minutes.
events.blurb: Write your name in Hangul using calligraphy brushes, ink, and hanji paper in a 90-minute workshop.

events.title: Sci-Fi & Fantasy Book Club
events.description: We'll be reading Elatsoe by Darcie Little Badger in honor of Native American Heritage Month. Sign up at the adult reference desk to get a copy. "Imagine an America very similar to our own. It's got homework, best friends, and pistachio ice cream. There are some differences. This America has been shaped dramatically by the magic, monsters, knowledge, and legends of its peoples, those Indigenous and those not. Some of these forces are charmingly everyday, like the ability to make an orb of light appear or travel across the world through rings of fungi. But other forces are less charming and should never see the light of day. Seventeen-year-old Elatsoe ("Ellie" for short) lives in this slightly stranger America. She can raise the ghosts of dead animals, a skill passed down through generations of her Lipan Apache family. Her beloved cousin has just been murdered, in a town that wants no prying eyes. But she is going to do more than pry. The picture-perfect façade of Willowbee masks gruesome secrets, and she will rely on her wits, skills, and friends to tear off the mask and protect her family." events.title: Documentary: UNAFF presents the Panama Deception
events.description: The Panama Deception documents the untold story of the December 1989 U.S. invasion of Panama; the events which led to it; the excessive force used; the enormity of the death and destruction; and the devastating aftermath. The Panama Deception uncovers the real reasons for this internationally condemned attack, presenting a view of the invasion which widely differs from that portrayed by the U.S. media and exposes how the U.S. government and the mainstream media suppressed information about this foreign policy disaster. The Panama Deception includes never-before-seen footage of the invasion and its aftermath, as well as interviews with both invasion proponents like Gen. Maxwell Thurman, Panamanian President Endara and Pentagon spokesperson Pete Williams, and opponents like U.S. Representative Charles Rangel (D-NY), Panamanian human rights workers Olga Mejia and Isabel Corro and former Panamanian diplomat Humberto Brown. Network news clips and media critics contribute to a staggering analysis of media control and self-censorship relevant to any news coverage today, particularly during times of war. Many local affiliates of PBS have broadcast the film, including KQED, but national PBS has refused to broadcast the film despite the Congressional mandate explicitly requiring that both sides of controversial issues be included in PBS's overall programming. Internationally, the film has been broadcast in Australia, Canada, Poland, Hong Kong, France, Spain, Portugal, the U.K., Iran, Israel, Finland, Switzerland, Mexico, Argentina, Japan, Norway, the People's Republic of China, S. Korea, Italy, Turkey, Russia, S. Africa, the Netherlands, the Philippines, Algeria, Malaysia, and Czechoslovakia. A ban on the film originally imposed by the Panamanian government was lifted in March 1993, following strong internal and international pressure. United Nations Association Film Festival presents documentaries on topical subjects. Jasmina Bojic, Stanford lecturer and International Documentary Film Festival UNAFF founder and director, facilitates discussions with filmmakers and producers. Registration is not required, but registering means you will receive a reminder email the day before.
events.blurb: Watch a screening of The Panama Deception, a documentary on the December 1989 U.S. invasion of Panama and its aftermath.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For December 6th: Topic: Epicurus's Challenge to Our Society: Raising a Tranquil Child "The wise man will marry and beget children, as Epicurus tells us in Problems and his work On Nature; but he will marry according to his station in life, whatever it may be." Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, 10:119. "Natural wealth is limited and easily obtained; the riches of idle fancies go on forever." Principal Doctrine 15. "Some men spend their whole life furnishing for themselves the things proper to life without realizing that at our birth each of us was poured a moral brew to drink." Vatican Sayings 30. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Ch. 17 (pp. 180-190). Some Questions to Discuss: In our society, how realistic is Emily Austin's Epicurean plan for raising a child? What are possible impediments to the realization of her plan? What are possible solutions for overcoming these obstacles?
events.blurb: Join a reading and discussion group about big ideas, including why many people tie success to constant hustle and going it alone.

events.title: The Thrifty Table: Creating Beautiful Holiday Centerpieces
events.description: Are you experiencing the "holiday guest stress syndrome"? Don't let the pressure of having a perfect tablescape wilt your holiday spirit! Join UC Master Gardeners Laura Westley, Sue Neufeld, and Bernie Day for an inspiring, hands-on demonstration designed to take the stress—and the high cost—out of holiday decorating. You don't need a professional florist or a massive budget to create a "wow" factor for your dining room. What You'll Learn: The Art of the "Found" Object: Learn how to scout your own backyard or junk drawer for unique textures, greenery, and accents that add character to any arrangement. Grocery Store Glam: Discover how to deconstruct those affordable supermarket flower bunches and reimagine them into high-end-looking centerpieces. Pro-Tips for Longevity: Get the inside scoop on keeping your flora fresh from the first toast to the final slice of pie. Why join us? Whether you're hosting a grand feast or an intimate gathering, you'll walk away with the confidence and practical skills to transform "ordinary" items into extraordinary focal points. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3947, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.

events.title: CNPS Talk #3: The birds, the bees, and a magic trait: The evolution of red hummingbird flowers in California, a talk by Prof. Justen Whittall
events.description: Why are so many of California's favorite hummingbird flowers red? From California fuchsia blooming in the fall to western columbine, scarlet bugler, and Indian paintbrush, our native flora is full of brilliant red flowers that hummingbirds love. But is red simply a color that attracts hummingbirds, or does it also help flowers avoid unwanted visits from bees? Join Santa Clara University biology professor Justen Whittall to explore how hummingbirds and bees see flowers differently, including a hidden world of ultraviolet colors invisible to humans. Drawing on recent research with his students and international collaborators, he'll reveal how these hidden pigments may help explain not only why hummingbird flowers are red, but also how new plant species evolve. Speaker Biography: Justen Whittall was born in Santa Clara and earned his B.S. in Biology from Santa Clara University, an M.S. from Oregon State University studying monkeyflower conservation genetics, and a Ph.D. from UC Santa Barbara investigating the evolution of California columbines. Following postdoctoral research at UC Davis on the evolution of California's serpentine-endemic plants, including blue-eyed Mary, wallflowers, and jewelflowers, he returned to SCU in 2007 as a professor of Biology. He works closely with undergraduates to uncover the mysteries of plant ecology and evolution, with research ranging from the conservation of rare Santa Clara County plants—including jewelflowers, columbines, liveforevers, and Hoita—to the evolution of flower color and hummingbird pollination in California's native flora. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3947, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.

events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: The group picks a graphic novel to discuss each month. The club is open to readers ages 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA. October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation. November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County. January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA. April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. The story follows a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. Borrow the books from Palo Alto City Library or through Link+. Search the library catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph.D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/

Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting Andrey Kurkov (Diary of an Invasion) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. What will we read next? It's anyone's guess. Members suggest books, and then vote on them. Join us the second Thursday of the month in the Embarcadero Room. Here's our reading list since January 2023. Our reading list for 2026 follows: My Friends by Fredrik Backman - January; The Wager: A Tale of a Shipwreck, Mutiny and Murder by David Grann - February; South of the Border, West of the Sun by Haruki Murakami - March; Trespassers at the Golden Gate: A True Account of Love, Murder, and Madness in Gilded-Age San Francisco by Gary Krist - April; The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui - May; The Wedding People by Alison Espach - June; Unlikely Animals: A Novel by Annie Hartnett - July; Say Nothing: A True Story of Murder and Memory in Northern Ireland by Patrick Radden Keefe - August; The Frozen River by Ariel Lawhon - September; We'll Prescribe You a Cat by Syou Ishida - October; What We Can Know by Ian McEwan - November; The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay by Michael Chabon - December. events.title: Non-Fiction Book Discussion – Finders Keepers: a Tale of Archaeological Plunder and Obsession
events.description: In December, the Cupertino Library's nonfiction book group will discuss Craig Childs' 2010 book Finders Keepers: A Tale of Archaeological Plunder and Obsession. Journalist Craig Childs documents his efforts to find and preserve precious and ancient artifacts from the American Southwest that could help answer questions about the people who made and used them. From archaeological digs in the deserts of Arizona and New Mexico to high-end art galleries and museums in New York and Boston, Childs had to protect the artifacts and himself from ruthless art smugglers, risking his life and freedom multiple times. Childs' book also asks who owns the past and its archaeological finds. An archaeologist may be praised for excavating an ancient site and sharing their finds with a famous museum. Someone who takes a precious relic from a museum because they believe it is sacred and belongs where it was found is called a thief. Which one is in the wrong? The Non-fiction Book Discussion group meets on the second Sunday of each month at 11 am. All meetings are held in Room 201B. Sponsored by The Friends of the Cupertino Library. events.title: Animal Friends: Meet a Chicken with Isabelle Cnudde
events.description: Did you know chickens can recognize over 100 faces, dream when they sleep, and even see more colors than we do? Join Project Humane Kind at the Palo Alto Children's Library as we meet Clorofil's Isabelle Cnudde and one of her feathered friends. Come discover their natural behaviors, their big personalities, and what makes them such cool animals. Coloring pages will be available for the attendees. Registration required. Note: Registrations will be released for standby attendees at the start of the program. Please arrive on time. As founder of Clorofil, an animal advocacy nonprofit and micro-sanctuary, Isabelle rescues chickens and gives them a safe home where they can just be chickens. Learn more about them at www.clorofil.org. Project Humane Kind teaches compassion and respect for living beings. Through humane education, they combat cruelty and indifference and bring awareness to the intelligent, social, and emotional depths of our fellow animals. Visit them online at www.projecthumanekind.org.
events.blurb: Meet Clorofil's Isabelle Cnudde and her chicken to learn surprising facts about how chickens see, dream, and recognize faces.

events.title: Celebrating Yalda Night
events.description: Join us for a special Yalda Night celebration with children's author Anahita Tamaddon and a reading of her book, Yalda Night! Experience the beauty of this cherished Persian tradition through a Yalda-inspired story, music, and a fun paper craft featuring one of Yalda's beloved symbols. Yalda, the longest night of the year, is a joyful celebration of family, storytelling, and togetherness as we welcome the arrival of winter. All craft materials will be provided. Children ages three and up, along with their adult caregivers, are invited to participate. Materials will be available while supplies last. While registration isn't required and doesn't guarantee a spot, it is recommended if you'd like a reminder about the event. برای جشن ویژه‌ی شب یلدا همراه با نویسنده‌ی کتاب‌های کودک، آناهیتا تمدن، به ما بپیوندید. در این برنامه با زیبایی‌های این سنت دیرینه‌ی ایرانی از طریق قصه‌ای با حال‌وهوای یلدا، موسیقی و ساخت کاردستی کاغذی با الهام از یکی از نمادهای دوست‌داشتنی یلدا آشنا خواهیم شد. شب یلدا، بلندترین شب سال، فرصتی برای جشن گرفتن در کنار خانواده و عزیزان، قصه‌گویی و با هم بودن و همچنین خوشامدگویی به فصل زمستان است. تمام وسایل مورد نیاز برای ساخت کاردستی فراهم خواهد بود.
events.blurb: Hear author Anahita Tamaddon read her book Yalda Night and make a Yalda-inspired paper craft.

events.description: Come and improve your mental and physical health in mindfulness meditation sessions led by Phuong Pham. Each session is 30 minutes of sitting meditation and 15 minutes of releasing meditation followed by 15 minutes of group sharing and Q&A. It is open to all levels of experience, and no registration is required. Participants are encouraged to bring their own yoga mats and/or meditation cushions. Chairs are available for those who do not bring them. Phuong is a Buddhist nun experienced in leading mindfulness meditation. See the library's event page to learn more about Phuong and find her videos on the library's YouTube channel.
events.blurb: Join Phuong Pham for guided sitting and releasing meditation, followed by group sharing and Q&A.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For December 20th: Topic: Becoming an Epicurean? "In other occupations, the reward comes with difficulty after their completion, but in philosophy delight coincides with knowledge. For enjoyment does not come after learning, but learning and enjoyment come together." Vatican Sayings 27. "We must not pretend to be philosophers, but be philosophers in truth. For we do not stand in need of the appearance of health but of true health." Vatican Sayings 54. "By love of true philosophy we are delivered from every disturbing and painful desire." Fragment 66. "The most important consequence of self-sufficiency is freedom." Vatican Sayings 77. "The impassive soul disturbs neither itself nor others." Vatican Sayings 79. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Chs. 23 (pp. 241-251) and 24 (pp. 252-266). Some Questions to Discuss: In your opinion, which of Epicurus's ideas, if any, have not lost their currency and would be beneficial to our society? What needs to be done to implement them? What challenges may their implementation face?
events.blurb: Join a reading and discussion group about big ideas, including why many people tie success to constant hustle and going it alone.

events.title: NeuroSphere: Neuroscience and More!
events.description: Come join the teen-led group NeuroSphere! This session will dive into the basics of brain function, fun activities to test your brainpower, and an introduction to future career opportunities. There will be snacks; feel free to bring a friend! We're a group of high school students driven by a passion for neuroscience and the wonders of the brain. Our mission is to inspire curiosity and spark a love for science in younger students by creating engaging, hands-on learning experiences. Through NeuroSphere, we hope to share our knowledge, connect with the community, and encourage the next generation of future scientists and innovators! Questions? Email neurosphereyouth@gmail.com.
events.blurb: Join teen-led NeuroSphere to dig into brain function basics and test your brainpower with hands-on activities.
