events.title: TLAB presents: STEM Sense Workshop
events.description: The mission is top secret, but we'll tell you this: it's all about balloon cars! Participants will build and experiment with balloon-powered cars, investigate the physics behind how they work, and apply that knowledge to improve their designs! Through demos, interactive learning, and hands-on challenges, students will practice asking questions, making predictions, testing ideas, and discovering how scientific concepts connect to the world around them. All materials are provided, and participants receive their very own kit to take home and continue exploring. Recommended for ages 8–11. We believe that STEM is about understanding why things work and applying that understanding for deeper exploration. Our workshops encourage students to think creatively, experiment freely, and learn through hands-on exploration. Learn more about us here: https://stem-sense.wixsite.com/stem-sense

events.title: Documentary Screening – Zora Neale Hurston: Claiming a Space
events.description: Join us for a screening of the PBS documentary Zora Neale Hurston: Claiming a Space, about a major Black American writer. Hurston is best known for her novel Their Eyes Were Watching God. The film explores her work as an anthropologist and how it influenced her writing. From the producer: "Raised in the small all-Black Florida town of Eatonville, Zora Neale Hurston studied at Howard University before arriving in New York in 1925. She would soon become a key figure of the Harlem Renaissance, best remembered for her novel, Their Eyes Were Watching God. But even as she gained renown in the Harlem literary circles, Hurston was also discovering anthropology at Barnard College with the renowned Franz Boas. She would make several trips to the American South and the Caribbean, documenting the lives of rural Black people and collecting their stories. She studied her own people, an unusual practice at the time, and during her lifetime became known as the foremost authority on Black folklore. Directed by Tracy Heather Strain, produced by Randall MacLowry and executive produced by Cameo George, Zora Neale Hurston: Claiming a Space is an in-depth biography of the influential author whose groundbreaking anthropological work would challenge assumptions about race, gender and cultural superiority that had long defined the field in the 19th century." Interested in delving deeper into Hurston's work? Join us for February's Short Story Social the Thursday following the screening to discuss her short story "Sweat."

events.title: Community Threads: Lunar New Year Felt Goat
events.description: It's the year of the goat! In this workshop, folks will make a felt goat for Lunar New Year. We will only be hand sewing in this workshop. Open to teens and adults only. events.description: "Nothing substitutes for the ability to build friendships with parents who are faced with similar parenting issues." events.title: Origami for Kids
events.description: Make designs like a sailboat, penguin, frog, or samurai helmet using colorful paper. Then decorate your origami with markers! events.blurb: Sit down with a volunteer reader for one-on-one or small group storytime that builds imagination and a love of books.

events.title: Rose STEM Arts & Crafts: DIY Sensory Bottles

With colorful glitter, beads, and more, these bottles are both fun and soothing. Rose STEM Arts & Crafts features cute, charming, and eye-catching projects, all with a STEM twist. Free. No registration required.

Children who are 10 years old and younger must be accompanied by parents.

events.title: Reading to Children

events.title: Mandarin Storytime

events.title: Sounds of South Asia: an Exhibit
events.description: This interactive photography exhibit showcases several musical instruments from the South Asian subcontinent. Each exhibit will have a QR code that allows participants to listen to the sound of the instruments played in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. They include stringed, wind, and percussion instruments passed down through generations, which are still played around the Bay Area. Come and enjoy this exhibit, which starts on November 14, 2026, and closes on December 5, 2026. The exhibit is brought to you by the South Asians in Silicon Valley initiative at the SJSU King Library. Through this unique initiative, the SJSU King Library records, preserves, and shares the living legacy of the South Asian diaspora in the San Francisco Bay Area. Website: https://library.sjsu.edu/sasv
events.blurb: See an interactive photography exhibit featuring musical instruments from the South Asian subcontinent.

events.title: Volunteer in the Historic Orchard with UC Master Gardeners!
events.description: The Historic Orchard is a 3.3-acre site planted in 1994 and located in Guadalupe Gardens just south of Taylor Street, adjacent to the Heritage Rose Garden and River Park trails. In the 1930s and '40s, almost everyone who lived here was engaged in the business of fruit production: growing, picking, packing, canning, selling, or otherwise supporting the industry. Today, with very few orchards remaining, this is a place where adults and children can come to experience a piece of local history. Fruit harvested from the Historic Orchard is donated to Second Harvest of Silicon Valley and local shelters. Help us maintain the River Park's Historic Orchard with activities including tree planting and pruning; disease diagnosis and treatment; sun scald prevention painting; sheet mulching; experimenting with different types of irrigation or ground cover; and grafting for improved pollination. Chaperones are required for those age 15 and younger. School groups or corporate teams must contact the Volunteer Coordinator at volunteer@grpg.org to schedule events. Address for parking: 438 Coleman Ave., San Jose, CA 95110; Meeting location: Historic Orchard (refer to the registration form for a map); Time: 9:30 AM - 11:30 AM; Recurring dates: Every Wednesday
events.attendanceNote: Advance registration is required through Guadalupe River Park Conservancy. Meet at Historic Orchard; see the organizer's registration form for the meeting map. Chaperones are required for those age 15 and younger.
events.blurb: Work alongside UC Master Gardeners in the 3.3-acre Historic Orchard in Guadalupe Gardens on a Wednesday morning.

events.title: Breathing & Meditation: The Natural Path to Better Immunity and Restful Sleep
events.description: Experience the soothing calm of meditation presented by library partner, Art of Living Foundation. Enjoy this free, one-hour session focused on managing stress and anxiety through simple, evidence-based techniques. These sessions are open to all adults and include optional light physical movement, breathing practices, and guided meditation. No prior experience is necessary. The agenda for a typical one-hour session is as follows: Optional Yoga Stretches (10 minutes): Light, beginner-friendly stretches; Will be offered based on participant interest. Breathing Techniques (10 minutes): Guided practice of calming breathwork; Techniques that can be used daily to reduce stress. Guided Meditation (20 minutes): Deep relaxation and mindfulness practice; Designed to calm the mind and promote inner peace. Experience Sharing & Program Info (10 minutes): Participants may share experiences; Information about the Art of Living and wellness programs; Optional: 3-minute video clip of past participant testimonials (if AV available). This program is geared to enrich the lives of adults and seniors. Registration is online.
events.blurb: Join an online one-hour session on breathing and meditation techniques for managing stress and anxiety, led by the Art of Living Foundation.

events.title: Noon Year's Eve Celebration!
events.description: Not planning to stay up until midnight on New Year's Eve with your little ones? Then join us for a "Noon" Year's Eve celebration! We will count down to noon on Thursday, December 31, complete with a "ball and bubble" drop. We'll ring in the new year with crafts, dancing and music, so bring your party hats and noisemakers! Come dressed in party attire if you'd like! This event will be held in the Adobe Room of the Mitchell Park Community Center.
events.blurb: Count down to noon with your little ones, with a ball and bubble drop, so no one has to stay up until midnight.

events.title: Alice, Formerly of Wonderland
events.description: Seven-time Emmy Award-winning writer Mark Saltzman illuminates the beautiful coming-of-age story revealing the truth behind the fairy tale between Alice Liddell—the real-life inspiration of Lewis Carroll's classic tale—and Prince Leopold, Queen Victoria's youngest son. Brimming with wit and emotional spark, this a cappella musical weaves between Victorian reality and Wonderland whimsy, revealing a tender connection shaped by duty, distance, and the ache of what might have been. Perfect for the holiday season, Alice, Formerly of Wonderland glows with warmth, longing, and just enough wonder to feel like a gift.
events.blurb: Watch the coming-of-age story of Alice Liddell and Prince Leopold unfold onstage at Lucie Stern Theatre.

events.title: Shane
events.description: A Wild West classic. Honoring the original while cracking it wide open, Karen Zacarias' storytelling is a living, breathing world of the American frontier as told by voices too often left out of the legend. The play unfolds in the vast Wyoming prairies, where families fighting for their land are pushed to the breaking point by forces determined to drive them out. Featuring Bay Area theatre veteran Aldo Billingslea as the fabled cowboy, Shane reminds us that true heroism isn't always about the fastest draw—it's about doing the right thing when it counts.
events.blurb: Watch a Wild West drama unfold on the Wyoming prairie, told through voices often left out of the legend.

events.title: Beautiful: The Carole King Musical
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.description: Feel the earth move under your feet! Soulful and irresistible, this feel-good musical tells the true story of the woman behind the soundtrack of our lives. From teenage songwriter to chart-topping legend, Carole King finds her voice in a world that wasn't always ready to hear it. Set against the vibrant music scene of the 1950s and 1960s, the journey follows love, resilience, the sort of friendships that shape a life—and a career that changed music forever. Featuring a thrilling lineup of iconic hits including "You've Got a Friend," "It's Too Late," and "You Make Me Feel Like a Natural Woman," Beautiful makes you laugh, tear up, and leave the theatre humming all the way home.
events.blurb: Watch the true story of Carole King's rise from teenage songwriter to chart-topping icon unfold in song at Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts.

From teenage songwriter to chart-topping legend, Carole King finds her voice in a world that wasn't always ready to hear it. Set against the vibrant music scene of the 1950s and 1960s, the journey follows love, resilience, the sort of friendships that shape a life—and a career that changed music forever. Featuring a thrilling lineup of iconic hits including "You've Got a Friend," "It's Too Late," and "You Make Me Feel Like a Natural Woman," Beautiful makes you laugh, tear up, and leave the theatre humming all the way home.
events.blurb: Watch the true story of Carole King's rise from teenage songwriter to chart-topping icon unfold in song at Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts.

events.title: We Will Receive Justice: A Local Indigenous History Book Talk
events.address: Central Park Library - Redwood Room, 2635 Homestead Road, Santa Clara, CA 95051
events.description: Two local university professors discuss their book 'We Will Receive Justice: Native Histories of the Collapse of the California Missions,' which explores how the ancestors of today's Ohlone community navigated the collapse of the mission system. Seating is first-come, first-served, and copies of the book will be available for purchase.
events.blurb: Hear two local professors discuss their book We Will Receive Justice: Native Histories of the Collapse of the California Missions.

events.title: FootGolf Tournament
events.address: Blackberry Farm Golf Course, 22100 Stevens Creek Boulevard, Cupertino, 95014
events.description: Enjoy a family-friendly evening of 9-hole Foot Golf, a fun twist on traditional golf where you kick a soccer ball toward the hole. Check in at 4:30 p.m., then tee off with a 5 p.m. shotgun start. Your registration includes soccer ball rental, green fees, snacks, and prizes for top overall scores. Perfect for all ages and skill levels.
events.blurb: Kick a soccer ball toward the hole in a 9-hole FootGolf tournament, with check-in at 4:30 and a 5 p.m. shotgun start.

events.title: Breakfast with Santa
events.address: Quinlan Community Center, 10185 North Stelling Road, 95014
events.description: You and your family are invited to a festive breakfast celebration with Santa! Enjoy delicious North Pole pancakes prepared by Santa's elves, take photos with Santa, and explore a holiday workshop filled with crafts and activities for children. Three seatings: 8:30 a.m., 9:30 a.m., 10:30 a.m. Registration opens in late July.
events.costNote: $18 for residents; $22 for nonresidents. Children under 2 are free.
events.attendanceNote: Preregistration is required for attendees ages 2 and older: $18 for residents, $22 for nonresidents. Children under 2 are free and do not need to register.
events.blurb: Eat North Pole pancakes, snap photos with Santa, and make holiday crafts with your family.

events.title: Environmental Education Center Open House
events.description: Drop by the Environmental Education Center (EEC) at McClellan Ranch Preserve every Saturday from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. for family fun and discovery. Meet the City's animal ambassadors, explore local wildlife, engage with preserve staff and park rangers, and enjoy hands-on activities that bring nature to life.
events.blurb: Meet animal ambassadors and try nature-focused hands-on activities alongside park rangers.

events.title: Community Emergency Response Team (CERT) Academy - Spring 2027 Los Altos Hills
events.address: 26379 Fremont Road, Los Altos Hills, CA 94022
events.description: Adults 18 and older can take this five-session disaster preparedness course at Los Altos Hills Town Hall. Evening classes run from 6 to 9 PM on April 5, 7, 12, and 14. Skills day is April 17 from 8 AM to 12:30 PM. Registration is required, and participants must attend all five sessions to graduate.
events.attendanceNote: Ages 18+. Open to people who live or work in County Fire's service area. Registration required. Attend all five sessions to graduate. Evening classes: April 5, 7, 12 and 14, 6–9 PM. Skills day: April 17, 8 AM–12:30 PM. Residents get registration priority.
events.blurb: Adults 18 and older can register for County Fire's five-session disaster preparedness academy at Los Altos Hills Town Hall.

events.title: Community Emergency Response Team (CERT) Academy - Winter 2027 Campbell
events.address: 1 West Campbell Avenue OCBH, Campbell, CA 95008
events.description: Five-session disaster-preparedness academy for adults ages 18+ at Campbell Community Center's Orchard City Banquet Hall. Evening classes: January 25 and 27, February 1 and 3, 6–9 PM. Skills day: February 6, 8 AM–12:30 PM. Registration is required; all five sessions are needed to graduate.
events.attendanceNote: Ages 18+. Open to people who live or work in County Fire's service area. Registration required. Attend all five sessions to graduate. Evening classes: January 25 and 27, February 1 and 3, 6–9 PM. Skills day: February 6, 8 AM–12:30 PM. Residents get registration priority.
events.blurb: Start County Fire's five-session CERT academy at Campbell Community Center's Orchard City Banquet Hall; ages 18+ and advance registration required.

events.title: Festive Night at NUMU
events.address: NUMU (New Museum Los Gatos), 106 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: The museum stays open late as a featured stop on the Los Gatos Chamber's Holiday Trolley route, with light refreshments, holiday crafts, music, and local art and history. Admission is $5 through Dec 10 and $10 day-of; always free for NUMU members, Los Gatos residents, and youth under 18.
events.blurb: Tour the museum after hours as a stop on the Los Gatos Holiday Trolley route, with holiday crafts, music, light refreshments, and local art and history.

events.title: Signing Santa
events.address: Quinlan Community Center, 10185 North Stelling Road, 95014
events.description: Deaf and hard-of-hearing children, along with their families, are invited to spend time with a Santa who understands sign language! Santa only communicates using sign language but an interpreter will be on-site to help translate for friends and family. Registration opens in late July.
events.attendanceNote: $5 residents; $6 nonresidents. Preregistration is required for every attending child and adult.
events.blurb: Meet a sign-language-fluent Santa with an on-site interpreter for deaf and hard-of-hearing families.

events.title: Tree Lighting
events.address: Quinlan Community Center, 10185 North Stelling Road, Cupertino, CA, 95014
events.description: Kick off the holiday season at the City's annual Community Tree Lighting! Enjoy the moment the tree is illuminated with hundreds of twinkling lights, live music from a local choir, and festive holiday cheer. After the tree lighting, families can visit Santa and take photos.
events.blurb: Watch the community tree light up, hear a local choir sing, and visit Santa for photos afterward.

events.title: Kampai for Christmas: Sake Tasting & Pairing
events.venue: Japanese American Museum of San Jose
events.address: Japanese American Museum of San Jose, 535 N 5th St, San Jose, CA 95112
events.description: A hands-on sake tasting class led by sake sommelier Meg Kawamoto of Sake Trend, covering sake history, brewing, and label reading. Guests sample 5-6 sakes paired with snacks, and bottles are available to buy. The event is 21+, tickets are required, and space is limited.
events.costNote: $115 general; $100 for JAMsj or Yu-Ai Kai members
events.attendanceNote: Ages 21 and up. Tickets required. Space is limited.
events.blurb: Taste five to six sakes paired with snacks while sommelier Meg Kawamoto covers sake history, brewing, and how to read labels.

events.title: Reading with Pets at Central Park Library
events.address: Central Park Library - Redwood Room, 2635 Homestead Road, Santa Clara, CA 95051
events.description: Kids in grades K-5 can practice reading aloud to a quiet therapy pet. Space is limited; reserve a time slot by calling 408-615-2916 during open hours or sign up in person at the Central Park Library children's desk, with sign-ups available 1 month before the event.
events.blurb: Read aloud to a quiet therapy pet if you have a kindergarten through fifth grader, with reserved time slots in the Redwood Room.

events.title: Will Anyone Buy It? Test Your Business Idea and Sales Pitch with AI
events.address: Central Park Library - Edinger Room, 2635 Homestead Road, Santa Clara, CA 95051
events.description: A hands-on SCORE Silicon Valley workshop on using free AI tools to research customers and competitors, write a sales pitch and outreach message, and build a seven-day plan to test demand. Attendees should bring a laptop and a business idea; beginners are welcome.
events.blurb: Use free AI tools to research customers, draft a sales pitch, and build a seven-day demand test; bring a laptop and idea.

events.description: Guided winter-themed painting workshop for ages 21+ and all skill levels, with materials and up to two complimentary glasses of wine included. Check-in is at 6:00 PM and painting starts at 6:30 PM. Tickets are $40-$50 and sales end December 3 or when sold out.
events.blurb: Paint a winter-themed piece in a guided workshop at the Triton, with materials and up to two glasses of wine included for ages 21+.

events.title: TRUST Information Table

events.title: Jane! An intimate exploration of Gilded Age excess and the enigmatic life and death of Jane Stanford
events.attendanceNote: Museum hours: Mon & Fri: 11 AM–6 PM; Thurs: 11 AM–8 PM; Sat & Sun: 10 AM–5 PM. Closed: Tues and Wed.
events.description: Curated by Associate Curator of European Art Patrick R. Crowley, Jane! celebrates the aesthetic and affective excesses of Jane Stanford, the Gilded Age founder and matriarch of Stanford University.
events.blurb: Tour the Cantor Arts Center exhibit on Jane Stanford's Gilded Age excess and mysterious death.

events.title: Electric Contrasts: the Art of the Detail
events.description: Electric Contrasts: The Art of the Detail brings together photobooks and magazines to show how the revolution of photography in the late 19th and early 20th centuries changed the history of art.
events.attendanceNote: Bowes Art & Architecture Library is closed Saturdays. Check the event calendar for hours. Visitors are asked to call 650-723-3408 for building and elevator access.
events.blurb: Browse photobooks and magazines tracing how early photography reshaped art history at the McMurtry Building.

events.title: Korean Indigenous Futures: The Art of Kim Bong-Jun
events.description: The East Asia Library at Stanford University will host a print exhibition by Kim Bong-Jun, a leading figure in Korean Minjung (People's) Art, from September 29 to December 11, 2026.
events.blurb: View prints by Kim Bong-Jun, a leading figure in Korean Minjung People's Art, at Lathrop Library.

events.title: Renewal
events.venue: King Library, Jennifer & Philip DiNapoli Gallery, 2nd Floor
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St, San Jose, CA 95112
events.description: Through powerful and deeply personal works of art, Halabi explores Holocaust remembrance, the tragedy of October 7, loss, resilience, and the enduring bonds of our shared humanity.
events.blurb: See Halabi's personal artworks on Holocaust remembrance, loss, and resilience in the DiNapoli Gallery on the second floor of King Library.

events.title: Emergent Properties: Decennial Reflections on Collections
events.description: In 2026 the David Rumsey Map Center celebrates its tenth year—a moment to reflect on how the Center has added value to scholarship on campus and around the world.
events.attendanceNote: The Map Center's drop-in hours are usually Wednesday through Friday and vary by week. Visitors need a government-issued photo ID to register at Green Library.
events.blurb: Browse the David Rumsey Map Center's decennial exhibit reflecting on ten years of its collections.

events.title: Patty Chang: surfacing
events.description: In surfacing, Patty Chang engages the ocean as a physical, geopolitical, and symbolic space, inviting you to consider the work of collection and recollection.
events.blurb: See Patty Chang's surfacing, an exhibit treating the ocean as a physical, geopolitical and symbolic space tied to collection and recollection.

events.title: California Current: Art and Histories from the Bay Area
events.description: How does a community stay rooted in a region that's constantly changing?
events.blurb: Walk through California Current at the Cantor Arts Center, an exhibit of Bay Area art and histories asking how communities stay rooted amid change.

events.title: Branner Library Book & Map Exhibit - Water in the West
events.attendanceNote: Visitors must present a valid, physical government-issued photo ID and sign in at the front desk. View Monday through Friday during Branner Library hours.
events.blurb: Browse Branner Library's book and map exhibit on water history in the American West.

events.title: Text Machines: Scarlet Thread of the Digital Order (1883-2026)
events.blurb: Browse the Text Machines exhibit on digital order at Green Library's Bing Wing.

events.title: A Vision of Paris: The Roxane Debuisson Collection at Stanford
events.attendanceNote: Bring a valid government ID and register at the entrance to Green Library to view the exhibition.
events.blurb: View the Roxane Debuisson Collection's vision of Paris at Green Library's Bing Wing.

events.title: In Focus: Asian American Art from the Collection
events.attendanceNote: Museum hours: Mon & Fri: 11 AM–6 PM; Thurs: 11 AM–8 PM; Sat & Sun: 10 AM–5 PM. Closed: Tues and Wed.
events.blurb: View Asian American art pulled from the Cantor Arts Center's permanent collection.

events.title: Natalie and James Thompson Gallery: Common Ground
events.address: One Washington Square, San José, CA 95192
events.blurb: See the Common Ground exhibit at the Natalie and James Thompson Gallery in ART 127 on the San Jose campus.

events.title: Human Rights Day Flag Raising Ceremony
events.description: Annual County ceremony marking Human Rights Day, with the theme "Making Humanity Together." It celebrates the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
events.blurb: Watch the county's Human Rights Day flag raising at the Government Center, themed "Making Humanity Together" and honoring the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
